ophelia_customer: Hey team — a customer hit a reproducible parser error when using streaming JSON from our /v1/generate endpoint. The client reports an unexpected end-of-input; final brace is missing. Happening ~30s into stream.

amanda_support: Sorry to hear that. Can you paste the raw bytes they got and the exact curl/fetch they used? Also which region and whether customer sits behind Cloudflare/CF Workers or a mobile proxy.

ophelia_customer: Sample from their app (redacted keys):
```
curl -v \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \ 
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"model":"open-zz","stream":true,"prompt":"{...}"}' \ 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate/stream
```
And the last chunk they received (truncated):
```
data: {"id":"req_123","object":"response","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"...\n","index":0}}]

```
Note there's no closing `}` and their JSON parser errors. They said no intermediate errors in logs, connection just closes.

amanda_support: Thanks. Do they see any proxy or LB logs showing a FIN/RST around that time? Does the client reconnect and get remainder?

ophelia_customer: They see TCP FIN from an IP that maps to Cloudflare edge, timestamp aligns with stream end. Client does NOT reconnect — parser fails because payload incomplete.

jordan_runtime: Looping in eng-runtime. This smells like chunk boundary + proxy idle timeout. Two quick things to check: (1) are we flushing trailing whitespace/newline after final chunk? (2) do we send an explicit sentinel (e.g., `data: [DONE]` or final JSON close) before closing the socket? Some proxies will cut the TCP when the keepalive window elapses and the final bytes still in kernel buffer.

ravi_sre: Agree. Also need timeline: request start ts -> last SSE event delivered -> TCP FIN. If it's ~30s consistently that lines up with Cloudflare default 30s origin timeout for long poll on some plans. Can customer share exact durations?

ophelia_customer: They measured: first chunk at 1s, last visible chunk at 29.8s, FIN at 30.1s. So yep.

jordan_runtime: OK that's a CF-origin cutoff. Workarounds: (a) emit keepalive SSE comment lines `: ping` every 15s to keep connection alive, (b) send an explicit final sentinel event before closing, (c) offer a non-streaming path for critical responses. We'll also look at our transport flush path — ensure `socket.shutdown()` occurs only after final bytes confirmed written and we flush kernel buffers.

amanda_support: Sent repro to oncall. Customer wants timeline and short-term workaround. Suggested they switch to non-streaming `stream:false` for now or add client-side tolerant parsing that waits for `\n\n` SSE boundary or times out and retries with a range/continuation.

deploy-bot: @jordan_runtime assigned to this thread (incident #INC-7412). :rotating_light:

jordan_runtime: Investigating. I can reproduce locally with a CF-like proxy that enforces 30s origin timeout. Repro steps: run a proxy that cuts connection at 30s, then stream a large response that completes at ~31s — client sees truncated JSON.

jordan_runtime: Minimal repro curl I used: 
```
# server: stream many chunks, finish after 31s
# client:
curl -v -H "Accept: text/event-stream" https://local-proxy.test/stream
```
Output ends with partial JSON.

ravi_sre: For mitigation we can: (1) default to emitting a zero-length SSE comment `: \'keepalive\'\n\n` every 10s from service side; (2) ensure last write uses `SO_LINGER` semantics or explicit flush + small delay before closing; (3) document proxy timeouts for customers.

jordan_runtime: I'll push a small runtime patch to emit keepalives for streams older than 10s and to write a final `data: {"done":true}\n\n` sentinel before initiating socket close. That should survive most proxy behaviours. Patch ETA ~4h for a staged rollout.

amanda_support: I'll reply to customer with repro explanation and a short-term workaround (use `stream:false` or client tolerant parsing + retry). Also ask them to test with `curl --no-buffer` and to capture TCP dump if possible.

ophelia_customer: Thanks — please cc their engineering contact, they need the temporary fix today. Also flagged as high priority on their side; they'll try `stream:false` as stopgap.

jordan_runtime: Noted. I'll post back here when the canary with keepalive + sentinel is deployed.

amanda_support: Thanks everyone. Adding follow-up: confirm if we should add doc blurb about Cloudflare origin timeouts and recommended client patterns.

ophelia_customer: Appreciate it. One more ask: can we add a server-side response header when we close early so clients can detect truncated streams (e.g., `x-rw-stream-complete: false`)?

jordan_runtime: Good idea — we can set `x-rw-stream-complete: true|false` in the close handshake. But proxies often strip or don't expose final trailing headers; sentinel event is more reliable. Still, we'll explore header to help non-streaming clients.

amanda_support: Closing loop: customer will switch to non-streaming fallback; eng-runtime to roll keepalive/sentinel canary; eng-sre to monitor edge CF metrics for 30s hits. I'll update this thread after canary. :white_check_mark:
